docs.text: Description ¶ This package provides the data-vault command, to interact with the dd-data-vault service via its REST API . Import jobs ¶ data-vault -r ROOT import list returns a JSON array of import jobs. Combine --pending , --running , --success , and --failed to select statuses; without flags all statuses are included. Use a positive --limit and optionally a nonnegative --offset to select a page; offset requires limit and defaults to zero. Results are ordered by creation time and job ID. data-vault -r ROOT import find-by-batch BATCH finds jobs for the exact batch path. The path may be relative to the server's configured dataVault.ingest.inbox or absolute within that inbox; paths outside it are rejected. Path normalization is lexical and does not resolve symlinks. Both commands output all job attributes by default. Use --short for objects containing only uuid , batch , and status . Empty results are [] ; errors go to standard error and return a nonzero exit status. OCFL objects ¶ data-vault -r ROOT ocfl list-objects returns a JSON array of object IDs, fetching every page by default. By default it includes both blocked and unblocked, and both ingested and uningested objects. Use --blocked or --unblocked to filter by block status, and independently use --ingested or --uningested to filter by ingestion status. The options within each pair are mutually exclusive. Supplying --limit or --offset returns only one page; the defaults are 100 and 0 respectively. data-vault -r ROOT ocfl is-object-blocked ID prints the blocked status as a JSON boolean on standard output. data-vault -r ROOT ocfl clear-object-block ID clears the block and writes Object is unblocked: ID to standard error, with no standard output. Either command accepts - or an omitted ID to read one ID from standard input. Errors are written to standard error and return a nonzero exit status. This changes the clear command's former false standard output; scripts must use its exit status instead. The service now returns 204 without a body instead of 200 with JSON false , so API clients must be updated or regenerated and deployed with the compatible service. These commands require a service implementing the 2.1.2-SNAPSHOT API contract; the snapshot API artifact must be available to build the CLI. Restaging failed imports ¶ Run data-vault -r <root> import restage-failed <selector> to restore failed object directories in the inbox without starting a new import job. The selector is an import job UUID or a batch path relative to or contained in the inbox. Prefix a UUID-shaped batch name with ./ to select it as a path. Missing or empty failed directories are no-ops; filesystem failures can leave a batch partially restaged. Messages and errors are written to stderr. Object version properties ¶ Object version properties are modifiable attributes of an OCFL object version, as defined by the object-version-properties extension. The object-property commands get and change them through the service, which validates every change against the property registry of the storage root before it is stored. The main use case is deaccessioning a dataset version. data-vault -r ROOT object-property get -i ID [-v VERSION] [NAME] prints the value of the property as JSON on standard output. Without NAME it prints all properties of the version. VERSION may be given as 1 or v1 and defaults to latest . data-vault -r ROOT object-property set -i ID -v VERSION NAME VALUE adds the property or replaces its value. Use --from-file FILE instead of VALUE to read the value from a file; trailing whitespace, such as a final newline, is removed. A value is interpreted as follows: A value that starts with { or [ is parsed as JSON. If it is not valid JSON, the command fails before anything is sent to the service. Any other value is taken as a string, so 1.0 is stored as the string "1.0" . With --json every value is parsed as JSON. Use this for numbers and booleans, and quote strings: '"foo"' . data-vault -r ROOT object-property set -f CSV_FILE sets a batch of properties. The CSV file must have a header with the columns OBJECT_ID , OBJECT_VERSION_NR , PROPERTY and VALUE . Values are interpreted as above; --from-file cannot be used in this mode. Each row is set separately: a row that fails is reported on standard error and the remaining rows are still processed. The command returns a nonzero exit status if any row failed. data-vault -r ROOT object-property delete -i ID -v VERSION NAME removes the property from the version. The service refuses a change if the resulting properties of the version do not conform to the property registry: an unknown property, a value of the wrong type, a missing required sub-property, or the removal of a required property. The reason is printed on standard error. Note that the whole version is checked, so a version that already lacks a required property cannot be changed until that property is set. Properties are set per version: setting a property on version 1 does not change later versions. Example: deaccession version 1 of a dataset, and reaccession it again. echo '{"datetime": "2026-08-04T14:37:52Z", "reason": "Invalid dataset" }' > details.txt data-vault -r ROOT object-property set --identifier urn:nbn:nl:ui:13-xxx --version 1 deaccessioned --from-file details.txt data-vault -r ROOT object-property delete --identifier urn:nbn:nl:ui:13-xxx --version 1 deaccessioned Values starting with @ A value that starts with @ is taken literally: @details.txt sets the value to the string @details.txt , it does not read the file. Use --from-file to read a value from a file. (The data-vault command does not support picocli argument files.)

docs.text: Installation ¶ Currently, this project is built as an RPM package for RHEL8 compatible OSes and later. The RPM will install the binaries to /opt/dans.knaw.nl/dd-data-vault-cli and the configuration files to /etc/opt/dans.knaw.nl/dd-data-vault-cli . The configuration options are documented by comments in the default configuration file config.yml . Building from source ¶ Prerequisites: Java 21 or higher Maven 3.8.7 or higher RPM Steps: git clone https://github.com/DANS-KNAW/dd-data-vault-cli.git cd dd-data-vault-cli mvn clean install
